zeros.title: How ndarray::Array::zeros works
zeros.description: An array of a given shape filled with zeros.

slides.caption: ndarray arrays are n-dimensional, like NumPy: Array1 is a vector, Array2 a matrix.
ones() and from_elem(shape, x) fill with other values.

ones.title: How ndarray::Array::ones works
ones.description: An array of a given shape filled with ones.

slides.caption: Works for any type with One + Clone.

from-elem.title: How ndarray::Array::from_elem works
from-elem.description: An array of a given shape filled with one value.

slides.caption: The value is cloned into every slot.
Like vec![x; n] for n dimensions.

from-shape-vec.title: How ndarray::Array::from_shape_vec works
from-shape-vec.description: Reshapes a Vec into an array; errors if the sizes do not match.

slides.caption: The Vec's elements fill the first row, then the next. 6 elements fit (2, 3) exactly.
A shape that does not match the length gives Err(ShapeError).

from-shape-fn.title: How ndarray::Array::from_shape_fn works
from-shape-fn.description: Builds an array by calling a function with each index.

slides.caption: The closure receives the index tuple.
Good for patterns and lookup tables.

linspace.title: How ndarray::Array::linspace works
linspace.description: n evenly spaced numbers from start to end (both included).

slides.caption: range(start, end, step) excludes the end.

range.title: How ndarray::Array::range works
range.description: Numbers from start up to (not including) end, by step.

eye.title: How ndarray::Array::eye works
eye.description: An identity matrix: ones on the diagonal, zeros elsewhere.

slides.caption: The array! macro is the common shorthand.
All rows must have the same length (checked by the type).

shape.title: How ndarray::ArrayBase::shape works
shape.description: The size of each dimension, as a slice.

slides.caption: dim() returns it as a tuple for fixed dimensions.

dim.title: How ndarray::ArrayBase::dim works
dim.description: The shape as a tuple (for Array2: (rows, cols)).

slides.caption: For dynamic dimensions it returns an IxDyn.

into-shape-with-order.title: How ndarray::ArrayBase::into_shape_with_order works
into-shape-with-order.description: Reshapes an array to a new shape with the same number of elements.

slides.caption: Fails if the element count differs.

t.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::t works
t.description: The transpose: rows become columns (a view, no copy).

slides.caption: t() swaps the axes by changing strides; no data moves.
Element (i, j) is now at (j, i).
Call .to_owned() to get a new array in transposed order.

get.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::get works
get.description: A reference to one element, or None if out of bounds.

slice.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::slice works
slice.description: A view of part of the array, chosen with the s![] macro.

slides.caption: s![] takes one range per axis, like NumPy slicing. Steps (..;2) and single indices work too.
The result is a view: no copy. slice_mut gives a mutable view.

slice-mut.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::slice_mut works
slice-mut.description: A mutable view of part of the array.

slides.caption: Changes go straight into the original array.
assign() copies another array into it.

row.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::row works
row.description: A view of one row of a matrix.

slides.caption: Panics if the index is out of range.

column.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::column works
column.description: A view of one column of a matrix.

slides.caption: A view with a stride, no copy.

select.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::select works
select.description: Copies the chosen indices along an axis into a new array.

slides.caption: Indices may repeat or be in any order.

diag.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::diag works
diag.description: A view of the main diagonal.

slides.caption: For non-square arrays, up to the shorter side.

mapv.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::mapv works
mapv.description: A new array with a function applied to every element (by value).

slides.caption: mapv passes each element by value (for Copy types); map passes a reference.

map.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::map works
map.description: A new array with a function applied to a reference of each element.

slides.caption: The element type may change: here f64 → bool.

mapv-inplace.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::mapv_inplace works
mapv-inplace.description: Replaces every element with f(element), without a new array.

fill.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::fill works
fill.description: Sets every element to one value.

slides.caption: Works on views too: fill part of an array.

iter.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::iter works
iter.description: Iterates every element in logical (row-major) order.

slides.caption: Works for any number of dimensions.
The index is a tuple for fixed dimensions.
Handy to find where a value is.
For floats, pairwise summation keeps rounding small.

mean.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::mean works
mean.description: The average of all elements; None for an empty array.

sum-axis.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::sum_axis works
sum-axis.description: Sums along one axis, removing it.

slides.caption: Axis(0) adds the rows together (one result per column). Axis(1) adds across each row.
The result has the other axis only.
None if that axis has length 0.

fold.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::fold works
fold.description: Folds all elements into one value.

slides.caption: There is no max() for floats; fold gives one.
Order is not guaranteed for non-contiguous views.

std.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::std works
std.description: The standard deviation, with ddof degrees of freedom removed.

axis-iter.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::axis_iter works
axis-iter.description: Iterates over sub-views along an axis (e.g. each row).

rows.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::rows works
rows.description: An iterable over the rows (the innermost lanes).

slides.caption: Works for any dimension: rows of every 2-D slice.

dot.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::dot works
dot.description: Matrix multiplication (or dot product for vectors).

note.text: rows of a × columns of b

slides.caption: Each result element is a row of a times a column of b, summed: 1×5 + 2×7 = 19.
Shapes must match: (m × k) · (k × n). With the blas feature it uses BLAS.

concatenate.title: How ndarray::concatenate works
concatenate.description: Joins arrays along an existing axis.

slides.caption: stack() adds a new axis instead.

stack.title: How ndarray::stack works
stack.description: Stacks arrays along a new axis.

slides.caption: All inputs must have the same shape.
concatenate joins along an existing axis.

to-vec.title: How ndarray::ArrayRef::to_vec works
to-vec.description: Copies a 1-D array into a Vec.

slides.caption: into_raw_vec_and_offset avoids the copy for owned arrays.

insert-axis.title: How ndarray::ArrayBase::insert_axis works
insert-axis.description: Adds a new axis of length 1.

slides.caption: Needed for broadcasting a vector as a row or column.
